nodes.label: Android Custom API Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: Preserves Clerk's multi-step authentication semantics, runtime capability gating, and separation between UI, orchestration, and API integration.

nodes.label: Android Prebuilt Compose Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: Uses AuthView and UserButton to minimize custom authentication logic while gating UI on asynchronous SDK initialization.

nodes.label: Client-Hydrated Auth Islands
nodes.rationale: Clerk hooks require a client directive; real-time authentication state should hydrate immediately with client:load.

nodes.label: Backend API Write Request Safety Gates
nodes.source_location: Mandatory checks before EVERY write request
nodes.rationale: Write requests require key and scope checks, confirmation, and irreversible deletion warnings to prevent unauthorized or destructive mutations.

nodes.label: Plan and Feature Entitlement Gating
nodes.source_location: Features vs Plans: When to Use Which
nodes.author: clerk
nodes.rationale: Gate capabilities by feature and whole tiers by plan so feature assignments can change without redeploying application code.

nodes.label: Background Token Message Passing
nodes.rationale: Content scripts cannot call Clerk directly because they execute on arbitrary origins, so authentication state must be requested from a background service worker.

nodes.label: Stable CRX Identity
nodes.author: clerk
nodes.rationale: A pinned manifest key keeps the extension origin stable across builds so Clerk allowed-origin configuration remains valid.

nodes.label: CLI Mutation Safety
nodes.rationale: Mutations should be previewed with dry-run and explicitly targeted before execution because agent mode cannot rely on interactive confirmation.

nodes.label: Deploy Handoff and Verification Protocol
nodes.rationale: Interactive production deployment remains a human-terminal step, while agents use read-only handoff and status commands to verify readiness.

nodes.label: Supabase Postgres Best Practices Release History
nodes.norm_label: supabase postgres best practices release history

nodes.label: Idle Connection Timeouts
nodes.rationale: Automatically terminate idle sessions to reclaim connection slots and release resources or locks.

nodes.label: Postgres Connection Limits
nodes.rationale: Bound connections and work memory according to available RAM to prevent memory exhaustion and preserve query performance.

nodes.label: Postgres Connection Pooling
nodes.source_location: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.rationale: Reuse a small pool of expensive database connections so many concurrent application clients do not exhaust Postgres.

nodes.label: Prepared Statements with Connection Pooling
nodes.source_location: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.rationale: Named prepared statements are connection-local, so transaction pooling requires unnamed statements, explicit deallocation, or session pooling.

nodes.label: Batch Inserts and COPY
nodes.source_location: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.rationale: Combining rows into one INSERT or using COPY reduces per-statement transaction and network overhead.

nodes.label: N+1 Query Elimination
nodes.source_location: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.rationale: Batch arrays or joins replace per-item queries with one database round trip.

nodes.label: Cursor-Based Pagination
nodes.source_location: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.rationale: Keyset cursors avoid scanning skipped rows and maintain stable performance at deep page positions.

nodes.label: Atomic UPSERT
nodes.rationale: INSERT ON CONFLICT performs insert-or-update atomically and eliminates races inherent in select-then-write flows.

nodes.label: Postgres Advisory Locks
nodes.source_location: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.rationale: Application-level coordination can use session or transaction advisory locks without manufacturing database rows solely for locking.

nodes.label: Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.source_location: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.rationale: Transactions that acquire resources in a common order avoid circular waits and deadlocks.

nodes.label: Short Database Transactions
nodes.source_location: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
nodes.rationale: Keep external calls outside transactions and hold row locks only for the minimum update scope to reduce contention.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED Queue Processing
nodes.source_location: Use SKIP LOCKED for Non-Blocking Queue Processing
nodes.rationale: Workers skip already claimed rows so queue processing can proceed concurrently without lock waits.

nodes.label: EXPLAIN ANALYZE Diagnostics
nodes.source_location: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries
nodes.rationale: Actual timings, buffer use, scan types, and loop counts reveal concrete query bottlenecks instead of relying on guesses.

nodes.label: pg_stat_statements Query Analysis
nodes.rationale: Aggregate execution statistics identify queries that consume the most total time or execute most frequently.

nodes.label: VACUUM and ANALYZE Maintenance
nodes.source_location: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
nodes.rationale: VACUUM reclaims space and ANALYZE refreshes planner statistics so Postgres can select efficient query plans.

nodes.label: Composite Indexes
nodes.source_location: Create Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
nodes.rationale: A correctly ordered multi-column index serves combined predicates more efficiently; equality columns precede range columns under the leftmost-prefix rule.

nodes.label: Covering Indexes
nodes.source_location: Use Covering Indexes to Avoid Table Lookups
nodes.rationale: INCLUDE columns can satisfy a query entirely from an index and eliminate heap fetches.

nodes.label: Postgres Index Types
nodes.source_location: Choose the Right Index Type for Your Data

nodes.label: WHERE and JOIN Column Indexes
nodes.source_location: Add Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
nodes.rationale: Frequently filtered columns and referencing foreign-key columns need indexes to avoid large sequential scans.

nodes.label: Partial Indexes
nodes.source_location: Use Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries
nodes.rationale: Indexing only rows that satisfy a stable filter reduces index size and improves matching filtered queries and writes.

nodes.label: Idempotent Constraint Migrations
nodes.rationale: Because PostgreSQL lacks ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS, migration code must query pg_constraint before conditionally adding a constraint.

nodes.label: Appropriate Postgres Data Types
nodes.rationale: Native types such as bigint, text, timestamptz, boolean, and numeric improve correctness, storage efficiency, and comparisons.
